da-false-claim.evidence: Re-read at f077b32. The remark gained the two properties dropped from prop:lp-dual-stability, a computation field (computations/confinement-operator-selection.py) and an authorNote saying both 'are properties of the specific Gram matrix at the substrate, checked numerically by the cited computation'. That is not so. (1) The remark gives kappa(G) ~ 7.0 as the condition number of the six-channel G, but the cited producer builds G under convention D and declares it singular: its witness has gram_det = -1.458e-17 and gram_inverse_kind = moore-penrose-pseudoinverse, and its code comments say the form is rank 5 and has no inverse. A singular G has infinite condition number, so kappa(G) ~ 7.0 contradicts the cited computation. toffoli-lp-stability-proof.md already records that under convention D the ratio is not a condition number. (2) The producer runs no LP/SDP solve and computes no shadow prices; its own comment says the 9 LP-dual placeholder keys were excised because 'those placeholders carried no shadow prices'. So neither the |y*_i| <= kappa(G)||t|| bound nor kappa(G) is checked by the cited computation. The sigma0 sigma1^-1 Gx row appears in lp-dual-stability-table-data.md, and the witness has a candidate for the single unit, but the bound is unchecked. These are the old claims 2 and 3, so the numbers are pre-existing; the PR newly asserts they are computationally checked.
